Pokemon Go 0.37 (with buddy system) blocks rooted Android devices. This works to get you back in... for now.

Punish the Innocent!

I woke up this morning to see if I was still in the gym across the street, and was confronted with this load of crap:

This device, OS, or software is not compatible with Pokemon GO.

Because apparently now

Rooted devices are not supported

-- https://support.pokemongo.nianticlabs.com/hc/en-us/articles/221958248

Also, Jailbroken iPhones aren't supported; dunno how they're gonna get back in.

Get Back

But the next level of Android rooting/controlling your phone is Magisk, which is the tool that gets you back into Pokemon GO on Android - it's basically a rootkit-level development framework for Android OS modders, and since it runs above & before everything else you can toggle root off temporarily and then your phone will think it's unrooted/stock, and that'll let Pokemon GO to start. You can then flip root back on when you're done.

It looks like Pokemon GO is using Google's "SafetyNet" to determine if it should allow a device to start the app. This is the same thing used to guard Android Pay, and why you usually lose the ability to use Android Pay after rooting a device or flashing a custom ROM. Incidentally, you can use Android Pay again if you apply your system-level modifications with Magisk.

You can check the SafetyNet status of your phone with this app.

Automate It

Magisk's root can be toggled on the command line... So with ~$5 for Tasker and AutoNotification, you can automatically turn root off when Pokémon GO is in the foreground, and back on when you exit the app: https://archive.is/zt8Ti

Me

I was running CyanogenMod 13 - a custom ROM that ships with root in the ROM and while access can be disabled it will always appear as a 'rooted' phone - on a Nexus 5X with an unlocked bootloader.

You should follow a real guide, but roughly, I did this:

  1. Backup System, Boot, and Vendor partitions with TWRP (On the Nexus device, if you get into a boot loop, restoring this backup should be enough to get you out of it. If you aren't comfy with mucking around flashing stuff to your phone, back up your Data, too)
  2. Copy that backup to my PC so I know I'll have it even if I have to wipe the phone!
  3. Install Magisk Manager APK.
  4. Install SuperSU APK, do not let it update the SU binaries, but do use it's "cleanup" tool to completely unroot my phone
  5. Turn off root access via CM13's settings
  6. Reboot to TWRP recovery
  7. Flash both Magisk v6 and phh-superuser from TWRP
  8. Wipe cache/dalvik from TWRP
  9. Reboot
  10. Open Magisk Manager and toggle root off
  11. Grant Magisk Manager root access via the phh-superuser prompt that pops up
  12. Open Pokemon GO
  13. See my babies again <3

The amount of horseshit this is is colossal!
